newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian accused of 35 murders yet to plea.
newsitem.headline: Australian accused of 35 murders yet to plea.

text.p: Australian Martin Bryant was on Monday remanded in custody until September 30 when he will enter a plea on charges of murdering 35 people in a wild shooting spree in April in the southern state of Tasmania.
Bryant, 29, was not present in the Hobart Supreme Court on Monday.
Judge William Cox remanded the case until September 30, when he said the indictments against Bryant would be formally presented and Bryant would be asked to enter a plea.
Cox said he expected Bryant to appear in court in person on that day. In May, Bryant appeared in court via a video link with his prison because of security fears.
Bryant is under tight security in Hobart's Risdon Prison.

On April 28, a sunny autumn Sunday afternoon, a lone gunman walked into the Broad Arrow Cafe at Port Arthur, one of Tasmania's biggest tourist attractions, and massacred 20 people as they ate their lunch.

Within an hour a further 12 people, including a three-year-old girl, were gunned down either outside the cafe, in their cars, or hiding behind a tree. By Monday, 35 people were dead in Australia's worst massacre by a lone gunman in modern times.

The killings resulted in a push by the Australian government to introduce tough new laws banning automatic and semi-automatic weapons. But the move has met stiff opposition from gun owners and rural-based politicians.
